{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{Use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2021}}
'''Deborah J. Hughes Hallett''' is a mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Arizona]]. Her expertise is in the undergraduate teaching of mathematics.<ref>{{citation|url=http://math.arizona.edu/people/dhughes1|title=Deborah J Hughes Hallett|work=Mathematics People|publisher=The University of Arizona|accessdate=2015-10-05}}.</ref> She has also taught as Professor of the Practice in the Teaching of Mathematics at [[Harvard University]],<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.thecrimson.com/article/1994/5/6/popular-math-ar-professor-will-return/|journal=[[The Harvard Crimson]]|title=Popular Math Ar Professor Will Return: Hughes Hallett Rejects Arizona Offer Despite Harvard Curricular Controversy|first=Sarah J.|last=Schaffer|date=May 6, 1994}}.</ref> and continues to hold an affiliation with Harvard as Adjunct Professor of Public Policy in the [[John F. Kennedy School of Government]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.hks.harvard.edu/about/faculty-staff-directory/deborah-hughes-hallett|title=Faculty Profile: Deborah Hughes Hallett|publisher=Harvard Kennedy School|accessdate=2015-10-05|archive-date=2015-10-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006111259/https://www.hks.harvard.edu/about/faculty-staff-directory/deborah-hughes-hallett|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Hughes Hallett earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1966, and a master's degree from Harvard in 1976. She worked as a preceptor and senior preceptor at Harvard from 1975 to 1991, as an instructor at the [[Middle East Technical University]] in [[Ankara]], [[Turkey]] from 1981 to 1984, and as a faculty member at Harvard from 1986 to 1998. She served as Professor of the Practice in the Teaching of Mathematics at Harvard from 1991 to 1998. She moved to Arizona in 1998, and took on her adjunct position at the Kennedy School in 2001.<ref>{{citation|url=http://math.arizona.edu/~atp-mena/HughesHallettBio.doc|title=Biographical sketch: Deborah Hughes Hallett|accessdate=2015-10-05|archive-date=2015-10-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006152229/http://math.arizona.edu/~atp-mena/HughesHallettBio.doc|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Work on calculus reform==
With [[Andrew M. Gleason]] at Harvard she was a founder of the Calculus Consortium, a project for the reform of undergraduate teaching in calculus. Through the consortium, she is an author of a successful and influential sequence of high school and college mathematics textbooks. However, the project has also been criticized for omitting topics such as the mean value theorem,<ref>{{citation|journal=PRIMUS: Problems, Resources, and Issues in Mathematics Undergraduate Studies|volume=4|issue=3|year=1994|title=Reflections on the Harvard calculus approach|doi=10.1080/10511979408965753|first=Patti Frazer|last=Lock|author-link= Patti Frazer Lock |pages=229–234}}.</ref> and for its perceived lack of mathematical rigor.<ref>{{citation|title=The Mathematics Education Reform: Why You Should be Concerned and What You Can Do|first=H.|last=Wu|journal=[[American Mathematical Monthly]]|volume=104|issue=10|year=1997|pages=946–954|jstor=2974477|doi=10.2307/2974477|citeseerx=10.1.1.38.6195}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=On the Harvard Consortium Calculus|first=Saunders|last=Mac Lane|author-link=Saunders Mac Lane|department=Letters to the Editor|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|year=1997|volume=44|issue=8|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199708/letters.pdf|page=893}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Calculus Reform—For the $Millions|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|year=1997|volume=44|issue=10|pages=1324–1325|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199710/comm-klein.pdf|first1=David|last1=Klein|first2=Jerry|last2=Rosen}}.</ref>

==Recognition==
Hallett was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1994.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|accessdate=2015-10-01|archive-date=2017-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

Hallett won the [[Louise Hay Award]] in 1998,<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.awm-math.org/hayaward/1998.html|title=8th Louise Hay Award|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|accessdate=2015-10-05|archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304055634/http://www.awm-math.org/hayaward/1998.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref> and was named a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1998.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|title=Historic Fellows|publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|access-date=2021-04-18}}</ref> She is a two-time winner of the ICTCM Award, in 1998 for her internet-based course "Information, Data and Decisions" and in 2000 for "Computer Texts for Business Mathematics".<ref>{{citation|url=http://ictcm.pearsontc.net/2011/ictcm-awards.html|title=ICTCM Awards|work=23rd Annual International Conference on Technology in Collegiate Mathematics|accessdate=2015-10-05|archive-date=2015-10-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006204440/http://ictcm.pearsontc.net/2011/ictcm-awards.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref> 

In 2005, she received a [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]].<ref name=web>{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|title=Recipients of the Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608175318/https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award |archive-date=June 8, 2024 }}</ref>

In October 2021, the [[American Mathematical Society]] named her as the recipient of the 2022 Award for Impact on the Teaching and Learning of Mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6840|title=Deborah Hughes Hallett receives 2022 Award for Impact on the Teaching and Learning of Mathematics|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|date=2021-10-19|access-date=2021-10-29}}</ref>
